extracted.intended_audience: general readers of Good Morning America; fashion consumers and observers of corporate communications
extracted.subtask_description: News coverage of a fashion brand's public apology and organizational response to a controversial ad campaign, summarizing statements, actions taken, and surrounding context. Useful for understanding crisis communications and reputational remediation steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal apology and acceptance of responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: “I want to personally apologize for the wrong artistic choice of concept for the gifting campaign with the kids and I take my responsibility,” — a senior creative issues a personal apology and explicitly accepts responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A direct, personal statement from a named leader that acknowledges error and accepts responsibility; helps humanize the response and indicates accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge specific inappropriateness
rubrics_metrics.description: “It was inappropriate to have kids promote objects that had nothing to do with them.” — identify and acknowledge the specific element that caused offense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Naming the particular choice or content that was wrong (rather than vague apologies) shows awareness of the harm and avoids minimizing the issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condemnation of the harmful subject and clarification of intent
rubrics_metrics.description: “I would NEVER have an intention to do that with such an awful subject as child abuse that I condemn.” — explicitly condemn the harmful subject and clarify lack of intent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Condemning the harm and stating lack of intent can help distance the brand from perceived endorsement; but must be paired with concrete actions to avoid being seen as deflection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commit to learning and engagement with relevant organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: “I needed to learn from this, listen and engage with child protection organizations to know how I can contribute and help on this terrible subject.” — commit to consult and work with experts/advocacy groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promising to engage stakeholders (e.g., NGOs, experts) demonstrates willingness to learn and repair; follow-through matters more than the pledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admission of systemic/process failure
rubrics_metrics.description: “Our current process for content validation has failed, and we recognize the need to do better,” — company-level admission that validation processes did not prevent the issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledging procedural breakdowns signals that the problem was not only an artistic lapse but also an organizational one; sets up expectation of process reforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational changes to prevent recurrence
rubrics_metrics.description: “We have reorganized our image department to ensure full alignment with corporate guidelines.” — take concrete internal organizational steps to fix decision-making and oversight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describing specific structural changes (department reorg, new approvals, governance) is stronger than generic promises and helps restore trust if implemented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal of offending content from platforms
rubrics_metrics.description: “We have immediately removed the campaign from all platforms.” — promptly take down the material that caused harm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Immediate removal shows responsiveness; documenting removal and where the content appeared provides transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pursue accountability through legal or contractual channels (when appropriate)
rubrics_metrics.description: “We are taking legal action against the parties responsible for creating the set and including unapproved items...” — indicate intent to hold third parties accountable for unapproved or malevolent contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signaling legal action can show seriousness, but it must be accurate and defensible; later decisions to drop suits (as here) may complicate public perception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Willingness to revise legal strategy based on new information
rubrics_metrics.description: Company later confirmed it would be dropping a lawsuit previously filed against production partners and a set designer after further information emerged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjusting course (e.g., dropping lawsuits) can indicate responsiveness to facts, but abrupt reversals should be explained to avoid appearing opportunistic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparent attribution of responsibility and description of roles
rubrics_metrics.description: The piece reports conflicting accounts about who controlled creative input — production company says it handled logistics and was not on set; set designer says Balenciaga representatives oversaw the shoot and props.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing clear facts about who did what (and sharing differing accounts) helps the public understand where breakdowns occurred; transparency reduces speculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reaffirmation of organizational values (safety and condemnation of abuse)
rubrics_metrics.description: “We strongly condemn abuse of children in any form. We stand for children's safety and well-being.” — restate core values and protective stance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reiterating values is important but must be backed by action; otherwise it risks being perceived as performative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely public communication and follow-up statements
rubrics_metrics.description: The company issued multiple statements (initial apology/statement on Nov. 22; further statements and actions announced afterward) to address the controversy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prompt initial responses followed by updates demonstrate an active communications strategy; timing and consistency are critical to controlling narratives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distancing from controversial collaborators when necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: The article notes the brand had previously cut ties with Ye after antisemitic comments and left Twitter after Elon Musk's takeover — examples of distancing from problematic figures or platforms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Removing or distancing from controversial partners can limit reputational spillover; communicate rationale so audience understands consistency with brand values.
